requirements.title: Global platform
acceptance_criteria: Global public routes preserve honest navigation, privacy, accessibility, analytics, and evidence boundaries; only a fresh server-signed proof can produce the account-deletion notice, whose copy distinguishes removed account-owned data from retained private operational feedback.

Global account navigation and the shared actor boundary accept only a canonical verified user or Supabase's explicit missing-session error; only Supabase's explicit missing-session error becomes anonymous, while missing clients, thrown or other Auth errors, contradictory results, malformed runtime responses, profile-query failures, and client transport failures become unavailable instead of Sign in and Sign up. Private pages and mutations fail closed; account-state-dependent DSA, System Design, homepage continuation, Interview Experience, browser-activity, and mock-review slices preserve public function while exposing unavailable rather than false-anonymous account state, and anonymous feedback can continue through its controlled public client without claiming a verified account association. The account-navigation client invalidates stale and unmounted responses, only an explicit SIGNED_OUT event forces anonymous navigation, re-verifies authenticated session events, preserves a last verified ready identity on refresh failure, and source-regresses compact live retry and conditional focus recovery without claiming rendered browser automation. Executable shared actor, identity, profile, response, and settlement matrices run in npm run test:auth-foundation.

Application and interview-round full create and edit actions strictly parse one complete singleton string snapshot before actor or persistence work. Missing, duplicate, file-valued, unknown, control-bearing, and oversized fields fail without mutation; create snapshots reject edit revisions, edit snapshots bind the exact loaded timestamp, and optional clears require explicit empty fields so incomplete direct actions cannot default status or erase private tracker content. Executable parser matrices and source-ordering checks run in npm run test:application-tracker.

Application full edits carry the exact loaded database revision into an owner-scoped timestamp compare-and-swap, so a newer quick status or other intervening save cannot be overwritten by a stale form. Query failures remain distinct from zero-row conflicts, while edit-only duplicate submission guards, retained drafts, atomic conflict copy, and a safe latest-version review path are source-regressed; real stale-write behavior runs in npm run qualify:database.

Application and interview-round deletion strictly parse one exact loaded revision before actor work and use only owner-derived revision-checked RPCs; authenticated direct table deletes and anonymous execution are denied, while stale, foreign, and missing targets return zero rows without mutation. Source-integration checks cover exact revision binding, synchronous duplicate guards, focusable pending confirmation, atomic conflict truth, and safe latest-version links; real stale-preservation, owner isolation, and intentional application cascades run in npm run qualify:database, rendered focus and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual, and hosted checks remain unchecked external-owner work.

Homepage account continuation distinguishes anonymous, ready (including genuinely empty), and unavailable states; shared-actor and authenticated continuation-data failures plus client transport and malformed-response failures cannot masquerade as signed-out or zero activity, account import requires a ready response, browser-local continuation remains available, and retry status and guarded focus recovery are source-regressed without claiming rendered browser automation.

Explicit browser-activity import strictly validates one bounded snapshot before actor work and uses owner-derived insert-only RPCs to report imported, existing, and failed outcomes without overwriting richer account progress. Only exact submitted snapshots confirmed imported or existing are removed from current primary and legacy browser state; concurrent edits, failed and unrelated activity, and saved plans remain. Duplicate, stale, and unmounted client settlements are guarded, while truthful live status and conditional focus recovery are source-regressed without claiming rendered browser automation; database atomicity, concurrency, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, and hosted RPC checks remain an external owner gate.

Shared study-plan and preparation-activity controls announce only confirmed account, browser-local, or visit-only outcomes, skip unavailable account actions, retain the bounded 160-item local write contract, and never apply stale results to a different plan or item. Account persistence from the shared activity control changes DSA and System Design status only through their owner-derived atomic quick boundaries, validates the returned canonical item ID, and cannot clear richer private progress fields.

Public-profile lookup treats only a successful zero-row result as not found; RPC failures remain on a temporary error path, account-disabled metadata stays truthful and noindex, and successful rendering remains limited to the approved safe public projection.

Branded public-profile links accept only bounded, credential-free canonical HTTPS GitHub or LinkedIn hosts; changed invalid values are rejected, unchanged legacy-invalid values are omitted from unrelated owner updates so they neither block edits nor get rewritten, and both the public RPC and application query independently mask unsafe legacy values.

Profile settings strictly parse one complete singleton browser snapshot and exact loaded revision before actor or profile work, then use only the owner-derived revision-checked full-save RPC. The account display-name action uses a one-field desired-state RPC under the same owner lock; direct authenticated profile updates are denied, revisions advance monotonically, two full snapshots from one revision accept exactly one coherent winner, and a concurrent display-name change cannot be erased by a stale full save. Executable parser, legacy-link, result, display-state, and source-integration checks run in npm run test:auth-foundation; database concurrency, grants, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, while hosted checks remain unchecked external-owner work. Source-integration checks cover manual-submit draft retention, duplicate guards, revision submission, earlier-snapshot truth, atomic live status, and safe conflict-link attributes; rendered draft retention, focus, and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual validation.

Literal and computed public links resolve only to static routes, exact registered members of finite dynamic route families, explicitly permitted runtime-dynamic routes, or real public assets; fabricated or unregistered members of finite route families fail closed.

Uncaught private Server Component failures reach the accessible temporary application error state, whose explicit Try again control uses Next 16's refetching retry contract; this source regression does not claim rendered browser execution.

Dashboard first-use focus and Behavioral story count come only from complete owner-scoped query results; query errors, malformed result shapes, invalid persisted focus values, and invalid counts surface one sanitized private-data error before first-use copy instead of defaulting to unsure or zero.

The preparation-settings private read renders editable defaults only after a complete owner-scoped preference result; a successful zero-row response remains a genuine blank state, while query failures, malformed result shapes, and invalid persisted enum values surface the sanitized private-data error before the form instead of presenting writable blank defaults.

Onboarding renders a saved reminder timezone or a genuine blank only after an exact owner-scoped preference result; a missing database client, query failure, malformed response, or invalid persisted timezone reaches the private-data retry boundary before the form, so browser timezone detection cannot turn an unavailable private value into a writable default. Executable result and source-ordering checks run in npm run test:account-lifecycle.

Preparation-preference saves parse one complete singleton role/focus/DSA-roadmap snapshot and its exact loaded revision before actor or persistence work; intentional empty choices preserve null semantics, while malformed fields fail without mutation. The owner-derived compare-and-swap accepts one coherent absent or matching-revision snapshot, advances revisions monotonically, preserves unrelated preparation fields, and makes a stale settings save conflict rather than overwrite a newer desired DSA roadmap. Legacy full-snapshot callers fail safely after migration-first deployment. Executable parser/result/display and source-integration checks run in npm run test:account-lifecycle; full/full and settings-versus-DSA concurrency, grants, legacy failure, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, while hosted checks remain unchecked external-owner work. Source-integration checks cover draft-preserving manual-submit wiring, duplicate guards, post-submit edit truth, revision advancement, atomic live status, and safe conflict-link attributes; rendered draft retention, focus, and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual validation. Complete-onboarding submissions separately parse their exact runtime intent and destination before actor, query, RPC, or revalidation work; setup skips ignore inactive optional choices and force those choices to null or false.

Display-name, email-change, password-change, and account-deletion actions strictly parse exact singleton runtime strings before actor, profile, Auth, or deletion work; non-FormData, missing, duplicate, file-valued, and unknown consumed fields fail without mutation while framework action metadata is explicitly ignored. Empty display-name removal stays intentional, deletion keeps exact confirmation and current-password proof where supported, and signup, recovery, and signed-in password change share the same 8–128-character letter-and-number policy. Executable parser and source-ordering checks run in npm run test:account-lifecycle and npm run test:production-hardening; rendered browser error announcement remains covered by the broader manual accessibility gap.

Password-reset navigation and mutation require a recent verified Supabase recovery authentication-method claim correlated to the same account; caller-controlled callback labels and an ordinary authenticated session cannot create that capability, and malformed, duplicate, file-valued, unknown, weak, or mismatched password fields are rejected before Auth work without a literal application recovery cookie.
known_gaps: Rendered browser accessibility and focus/history coverage remains incomplete.
Hosted production evidence remains an external owner gate.

Executable parser, result, and pending-edit display-state matrices plus source-integration checks cover draft-preserving manual-submit wiring, synchronous duplicate protection, exact-snapshot truth, atomic live-region semantics, focus-preserving pending/conflict controls, and the conflict-only safe same-attempt recovery link in npm run test:system-design-workspace; rendered draft retention, conflict recovery, focus, and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual validation.

Full System Design item-progress edits strictly parse one canonical item/type, complete rich-field snapshot, explicit bookmark presence, and an absent sentinel or persisted revision before account work. The owner-scoped database operation serializes the same item key as status-only quick saves and uses insert-if-absent or timestamp compare-and-swap, so stale full/full, full/quick, and absent/import races cannot silently overwrite a winner; only validated success advances the revision, refreshes, and emits account analytics. Source-integration checks cover the component's draft-preserving manual-submit wiring, duplicate guard, live-region semantics, focus-preserving pending control, and a conflict-only latest-version link whose href is correlated to the canonical public item and whose new-tab attributes are safe; rendered draft retention, conflict recovery, and focus behavior remain browser/manual validation. Executable and source coverage runs in npm run test:system-design-workspace and npm run test:unified-progress, local concurrency/privacy runs in npm run qualify:database, and hosted RPC verification remains an unchecked external-owner step.

System Design attempt deletion strictly parses the displayed attempt, canonical problem, exact integer revision, and empty action form before account or persistence work, then accepts only a correlated one-row result. Save and delete share an owner/attempt lock, so a concurrent save-versus-delete race has one winner while stale, problem-mismatched, foreign, missing, malformed, and failed deletes preserve the worksheet. The legacy delete fails safely and only the revision-aware confirmation exposes conflict recovery. Executable parser/result and source-integration checks run in npm run test:system-design-workspace; database concurrency, grant, legacy, and owner-privacy evidence runs in npm run qualify:database; hosted races plus rendered confirmation focus and recovery remain unchecked external/browser-manual validation.

requirements.title: Interview Playbook
acceptance_criteria: Planning and round guidance preserve existing evidence boundaries and public handoffs.

Custom preparation-task creation strictly parses one exact bounded single-line title and bound round/application identities before actor or persistence work, then validates the returned task identity. The owner-derived database RPC serializes each owner/round before checking the 12-task cap and assigning the next position, so concurrent additions cannot exceed the cap or create duplicate positions; direct inserts, anonymous callers, malformed titles, and foreign or missing rounds fail without changing the owner list. Executable parser/result and source-integration checks run in npm run test:interview-preparation-hub; database cap-edge concurrency, grants, validation, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, while hosted verification remains an unchecked external-owner step.

Interview-round full edits carry the exact loaded database revision into an owner- and application-scoped timestamp compare-and-swap, so a newer completion or other intervening save cannot be overwritten by a stale form. Query failures remain distinct from zero-row conflicts, while edit-only duplicate submission guards, retained drafts, atomic conflict copy, and a safe latest-version review path are source-regressed; real stale-write behavior runs in npm run qualify:database.

Owner-scoped round preparation counts preserve distinct ready, genuinely untouched, and unavailable states across Dashboard, Application Detail, and Interview Playbook; empty input resolves before actor work, a nonempty request without an actor or any failed count query cannot render zero, start-plan, or not-started claims, and the shared retry exposes guarded pending, live-status, and responsive source contracts. Only an explicit successful retry announces that preparation progress loaded, and its source-regressed focus recovery targets the connected success status after a frame only when the retry trigger owned focus and no newer focus claim exists; rendered focus behavior remains browser/manual validation.

Checklist mutations parse one exact round identifier, canonical item identifier, and boolean desired membership before actor or persistence work; the route submits no whole-array snapshot, and the owner-scoped database function serializes and idempotently changes only that item while preserving independent checklist progress and returning the owning application for revalidation. The retired legacy snapshot RPC fails safely before any checklist or text mutation, cross-owner changes remain forbidden, executable and source contracts run in npm run test:interview-preparation-hub, database behavior remains assigned to npm run qualify:database, and hosted RPC verification remains an unchecked external-owner step.

Custom preparation-task completion parses one exact round, task, and boolean desired state before actor or persistence work; the control binds the visible inverse state rather than a flip-current command, and the owner-derived RPC locks and correlates the exact round/task pair. Deletion strictly parses the displayed round, task, and database revision first, then uses the same owner/task lock so concurrent completion and deletion accept exactly one outcome; stale, missing, foreign, and round-mismatched deletes return the same zero-row conflict without mutation, direct deletion is denied, and both retired task RPCs fail safely. Executable parser, result, and source-integration checks run in npm run test:interview-preparation-hub; database concurrency, grants, lifecycle, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, while hosted verification remains an unchecked external-owner step. Source-integration checks cover the revision-bound confirmation, manual-submit duplicate guard, atomic status semantics, retained focus, and safe conflict-link attributes; rendered conflict recovery, focus, and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual validation.

Round-preparation notes and completed-round reflections strictly parse exact browser fields, bound round/application UUIDs, and an explicit absent or loaded family revision before actor or persistence work, then use only the owner-derived revision-checked notes or reflection RPC. The two text families use independent revisions under the round lock shared with checklist updates: stale, missing, and foreign saves return zero rows without mutation, one of two same-revision snapshots wins coherently, notes and reflection can both save without invalidating each other, checklist state is preserved, and the legacy snapshot RPC fails safely. Executable parser, result, display-state, and source-integration checks run in npm run test:interview-preparation-hub; database concurrency, grants, lifecycle, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, while hosted verification remains an unchecked external-owner step. Source-integration checks cover manual-submit draft retention, duplicate guards, revision submission, earlier-snapshot truth, pending/live-region semantics, and safe conflict-link attributes; rendered draft retention, focus, and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual validation.

Reminder-preference saves strictly parse one complete checkbox snapshot and an explicit absent or loaded revision before availability, actor, or persistence work, then use only the owner-derived revision-checked RPC. Stale full saves and stale absence retries return conflicts without changing preferences or reminder rows; successful saves advance the revision and resynchronize future reminders atomically under the owner lock shared with round changes, while repeated completed-onboarding submissions cannot bypass that boundary and the legacy snapshot RPC fails safely. Executable parsing, result correlation, and source-integration checks run in npm run test:interview-calendar-reminders; database concurrency, rollback, grants, and owner isolation run in npm run qualify:database, and hosted checks remain an unchecked external-owner step. Source-integration checks cover manual-submit draft retention, duplicate guards, revision submission, pending/live-region semantics, and safe conflict recovery-link attributes; rendered draft retention and assistive-technology behavior remain browser/manual validation.

Interview Playbook diagnostic saves strictly parse one complete browser form and an explicit absent or loaded revision before availability, actor, or persistence work, then use only the owner-derived revision-checked aggregate RPC. Zero-row stale saves are conflicts, successful saves advance the revision, and the legacy whole-aggregate RPC fails safely; reads use one strict coherent aggregate snapshot that distinguishes genuine absence from failed or malformed snapshot-RPC results and preserves canonical child ordering. Shared actor failures now fail closed as unavailable before this private query or mutation boundary. Executable parser, snapshot, result, display-state, and source-integration checks run in npm run test:interview-playbook-diagnostic-inputs; database concurrency, coherent-read, grants, and owner-isolation checks run in npm run qualify:database, while hosted checks remain unchecked external-owner work. requirements.notes: All 13 distinct dossiers have source IDs and review dates; private attempt storage is owner-scoped and excluded from analytics.

requirements.title: DSA language coverage
acceptance_criteria: Published language guides have reviewed semantics, examples, pitfalls, responsive rendering, and compile or parse evidence.
known_gaps: C++, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Go remain coming soon.
C++ placement and approved source artifacts remain unresolved.

requirements.title: DSA curriculum shells
acceptance_criteria: Every shell remains honest and noindex until reviewed instructional content and acceptance evidence are present.
known_gaps: Thirty-four curriculum records remain explicit coming-soon states.

requirements.title: Company Guide coverage and provenance
acceptance_criteria: Every published company claim resolves to current attributable evidence or is clearly labeled as editorial recommendation or candidate report.
known_gaps: Ten normalized priority records exist, but claim-level provenance, current verification, and an approved expansion set remain incomplete.

requirements.title: Behavioral curriculum depth
acceptance_criteria: Sixteen substantial sourced lessons, framework comparisons, annotated examples, exercises, adaptive probes, and evaluator rules publish through finite routes.
The imported repository synthesis, exact descriptive rubric, source records, privacy/inference boundaries, and rendered desktop/mobile review provide the approved evidence policy.
requirements.notes: The former curriculum-depth gap is closed by the published sixteen-lesson sequence, six approved synthesis artifacts, adaptive follow-up engine, descriptive rubric, and acceptance tests.

requirements.title: Interview Playbook curriculum depth
acceptance_criteria: Expanded frameworks and stage-specific guidance map to imported sources, acceptance criteria, and privacy boundaries.
requirements.notes: The public lifecycle framework, adaptive plan contract, privacy boundaries, imported artifacts, and current source hierarchy close the tracked depth gap.

requirements.title: Round-execution dossier provenance
acceptance_criteria: Each dossier exposes a reviewed methodology and claim-to-source mapping before substantive guidance is promoted.
requirements.notes: Every full dossier renders its reviewed source-grounded, employer-example, and editorial-synthesis claim groups with explicit boundaries.

requirements.title: Technical-presentation guide
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed audience, role scope, source set, examples, and editorial specification precede publication.
requirements.notes: The published guide covers audience, purpose, structure, evidence, role-level overlays, questions, recovery, accessibility, integrity, examples, and source methodology.

requirements.title: Peer mock facilitation
acceptance_criteria: Product, privacy, safety, moderation, evidence, and trust specifications precede any peer network behavior.
known_gaps: The current product intentionally does not match, schedule, verify, or guarantee peers.

requirements.title: Low-Level Design rehearsal
acceptance_criteria: An approved rehearsal flow, rubric, persistence boundary, and self-review-versus-evaluator decision precede implementation.
known_gaps: Core lessons and practices exist, but the rehearsal and evaluator workflow is unspecified.

requirements.title: AI Basics beginner scope
acceptance_criteria: Founder approval, audience definition, artifact import, and source review precede route architecture and curriculum work.
known_gaps: Learning outcomes, audience, relationship to ML Design, exercises, and source policy remain unresolved.

requirements.title: AI for Kids
acceptance_criteria: No implementation begins without new product authorization and child-safety, privacy, legal, pedagogy, moderation, and source review.
known_gaps: Explicitly excluded from the current product scope.

requirements.title: General Core Concepts scope
acceptance_criteria: A product definition identifies the subject, audience, concept map, and relationship to existing System and ML Design concepts.
known_gaps: The requested subject and audience are ambiguous; existing scoped concepts must not be relabeled.

requirements.title: Employer-specific referral policy guidance
acceptance_criteria: Employer-specific claims publish only from current official employer policy with legal/editorial scope and freshness rules.
known_gaps: The current local toolkit deliberately directs users to official employer rules and makes no employer-policy claims.
